nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience (PCN) toolkit version 0.27 for normative modeling of resting state connectivity data. The normative model was generated using data from approximately 22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (age range 2-100 years). The specific algorithm underlying the PCN toolkit implementation was not explicitly specified in the paper.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Here, we used the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience (PCN) toolkit (version 0.27), a publicly available Python package, for normative modeling of resting state connectivity data. The normative model was generated using resting state connectivity data from approximately 22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (age range (yrs): 2-100).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled resting-state functional connectivity using the Yeo-17 functional network parcellation atlas, resulting in a functional connectivity matrix of 136 connectivity values (between 17 networks).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Functional brain networks were then parcellated using the Yeo-17 functional network parcellation atlas, resulting in a functional connectivity matrix of 136 connectivity values.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model was built from healthy individuals spanning ages 2-100 years, with age as the primary explanatory variable for generating normative reference curves. The study utilized pre-built normative models from the PCN toolkit, calibrated with local healthy control data.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The normative model was generated using resting state connectivity data from approximately 22,000 healthy individuals across the lifespan (age range (yrs): 2-100). Healthy control data collected in this project were used for calibration of the normative reference curves
